Subject: Complaint - CHAPS payment for our house completion sent a day late - costs incurred

Dear Sir or Madam,

I am writing to make a formal complaint, and I apologise in advance because this is going to be a long email, but I want you to have the full picture because frankly I have had to explain it to four different people on the phone already and I am not doing it again.

First of all some background. I have been a customer of Harbour & Vale since 1998 when I opened a student account at the old branch on the High Street in Harrogate (which you closed in 2021, which I was not happy about at the time either, but that is another story). My late father [PERSON_1] banked with you for over forty years before that. I have always recommended you to friends. I even put up with the app redesign last year which, to be honest, made it much harder to find anything. I mention all of this so you understand I am not someone who complains for the sake of it. The only other time I have ever complained was in 2019 when my card was cloned in Spain and that was sorted out very quickly and I was happy with how it was handled.

So. My wife [PERSON_2] and I have been buying a house at [ADDRESS_1], Knaresborough, [POSTCODE_1], for most of this year. It has been a long process with a chain of four and we finally had completion fixed for Thursday 15th October. Our solicitor, [PERSON] at Wetherby Lane Solicitors, told us very clearly that the balance of the purchase money from us (£74,250, which was the proceeds from our savings and a gift from [PERSON_2]'s parents) had to be in their client account by 12 noon on the Thursday at the latest, otherwise completion could not happen that day.

On the Tuesday (13th) I phoned your helpline to ask how to send such a large amount, because the online banking limit for normal transfers is lower than that. I was told to use the CHAPS option in online banking, that it would arrive the same day as long as it was set up before the cut-off, and that it might be checked by your security team. I said fine, that makes sense.

On Wednesday 14th at about 3.20pm I set up the CHAPS payment in online banking with the value date of Thursday 15th, exactly as I had been told. I triple checked the sort code and account number with the solicitor's letter. The screen said 'Your payment is being reviewed. We may call you to confirm it.' Nobody called me on the Wednesday. I assumed that meant everything was fine.

On Thursday morning at about 9am [PERSON] emailed to say nothing had arrived. I rang you at 9.15 and spoke to a lady called [STAFF_2] who said the payment was 'with the payments team for checks' and it 'should go today'. I asked if I could do anything to speed it up, confirm it was me, anything, and she said no, the team would call me. I rang again at 12.40 and was told the same thing. I rang again at 2.10pm and was told that the cut-off for the day had now passed and it would go first thing Friday. At no point did anybody from your payments team actually call me, even though I was sitting by the phone all day with my passport and every document you could possibly want.

The money finally left at about 10am on Friday 16th, after someone from your team rang me at 9.50 and asked me two questions which took less than a minute. Two questions! That could have happened on Wednesday afternoon.

Because the money was late, we could not complete on the Thursday. The removal firm, Dalesway Removals, had already loaded the van on the Thursday morning (we had to be out of our old house at [CUSTOMER] because our buyers were completing too), so they had to keep everything in the van overnight in their depot and come back on Friday, which they charged us for. We had nowhere to sleep on the Thursday night, so we had to book two rooms at a hotel off the A1 for us and the children ([PERSON_4] is 9 and [PERSON_5] is 6, they were in bits about it, they had been so excited about their new bedrooms). We also had to put our dog in kennels for the night because the hotel would not take dogs. And we had to buy all our meals out because everything we owned was in a van.

The costs are as follows:
- Dalesway Removals, extra day and overnight storage: £585.00
- Hotel, two rooms, Thursday night: £342.00
- Kennels, one night (emergency booking): £95.00
- Meals and essentials on Thursday and Friday: £118.00
Total: £1,140.00

I have receipts for all of these and I can send them to you.

We eventually completed at about 3.30pm on the Friday. [PERSON] has also told me that the sellers' solicitors could, in theory, have charged us interest for late completion under the contract. Thankfully they have not done so, but it was another worry on top of everything else.

I want to be absolutely clear that this was not my fault. I followed your instructions exactly. I set the payment up the day before, well before the cut-off. You told me you might call me and you did not. When I rang you three times on the Thursday, nobody was able to do anything. It feels like the payment was just sitting in somebody's queue.

I also want to say that the stress this caused my family on what should have been one of the best days of our lives was enormous. [PERSON_2] was in tears in the car outside the old house. My son kept asking if we were homeless now. I know you cannot put a price on that but I think you should at least recognise it.

What I would like from you:
1. The £1,140 of costs refunded to me.
2. An explanation of why the payment was held for two days when the check took one minute, and why nobody called me on the Wednesday as the screen said they might.
3. Some compensation for the stress and inconvenience.
4. An apology.

As I say, I have been a loyal customer for nearly thirty years and my father before me, and I would like to stay one, but I need to know this has been taken seriously. Please do not send me a standard letter saying you are 'sorry to hear about my experience'. I have had enough of those from the solicitors, the estate agents and the removal firm over the past few months.

For reference, the payment came from my current account, [ACCOUNT]. My phone number is [CUSTOMER_PHONE] and my personal email is [EMAIL_1], which is better than post because we are still waiting for our mail redirection to start working properly.

Thank you for reading this far.

Yours faithfully,

[CUSTOMER]

Task status: OPEN, unassigned. 15/10/2026 16:00 CHAPS cut-off passed, payment rolled to next business day. 16/10/2026 09:51 Verification call completed, customer confirmed payment. 16/10/2026 10:04 CHAPS sent. Status: COMPLETE.

Complaint rec'd by email 19/10 from [CUSTOMER] re late CHAPS for house completion. Very long email, key pts: CHAPS £74,250 set up in OLB Weds 14/10 for value Thurs 15/10, held for HVP review, verif call task not actioned till Fri 16/10, completion slipped a day. Claims £1,140 costs (removals, hotel, kennels, meals), receipts available. Also wants explanation, compensation for distress, apology. Called [CUSTOMER_PHONE] on 20/10 14:05 no answer, VM left. - [STAFF_1]
